questions.q:
In the given food chain, if plants absorb 1000 Joules of light energy, then how much energy is available for Lion? 

   Plants       →      Deer          →     Lion
(Producer)        (Herbivore)       (Carnivore)
questions.solution:
10 Joules

Explanation:

In an ecosystem, energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next. However, only 10% of the energy is passed on, while 90% is lost due to heat, respiration, and metabolic activities. This principle is known as Lindeman’s 10% Law of Energy Transfer.

Step-by-Step Energy Transfer:

Energy transfer from Plants to Deer (Herbivores):

  • Plants absorb 1000 Joules of light energy from the sun.
  • Only 10% of this energy is passed to the Deer, while 90% is lost.

Energy available to Deer = `10/100 xx 1000` = 100 Joules

Energy transfer from Deer to Lion (Carnivores):

  • The Deer has 100 Joules of energy.
  • Only 10% of this energy is passed to the Lion, while 90% is lost.

Energy available to Lion = `10/100 xx 100` = 10 Joules

questions.q: Which one of the following does not evolve further?
questions.solution:
Climax community

Explanation:

The ecosystem is initially occupied by the pioneer species. As time passes, species diversity increases, giving way to more complex organisms. Eventually, it leads to a climax community. The climax community does not evolve further.

questions.q:
Give a scientific reason:

The pyramid of energy is always upright.



Explain why, the flow of energy in the ecosystem is said to be unidirectional.



Give scientific reasons:

Ozone present in the stratosphere is called as “good ozone”.
questions.solution:
The pyramid of energy is always upright; it can never be inverted. Every step from one trophic level to the next results in a loss of energy in the form of heat.



Energy enters plants from the sun during food production through photosynthesis. This energy is then passed on from one organism to another in a food chain. The energy given out by organisms as heat is lost in the environment and does not return to be used by plants again. This makes the flow of energy in an ecosystem unidirectional. Thus, the flow of energy in an ecosystem is said to be unidirectional because the energy lost as heat from the organisms in a food chain cannot be reused by plants in photosynthesis.



Ozone present in the stratosphere is called as good ozone as this ozone absorbs UV rays from the sun which is harmful to living organisms. DNA and proteins of living organisms absorb UV rays and its high energy breaks down the chemical bonds within these molecules. This causes damage to skin cells and skin cancer of different types. A high dose of UV-B causes inflammation of the cornea called snow-blindness cataracts. This all is prevented by this stratosphere ozone as it absorbs UV rays.

questions.q: Explain the carbon cycle with the help of a simplified model.
questions.solution:
Carbon cycle in nature:

(i) The main source of carbon in this Universe is CO2 which is dissolved in water and present in air (0.03–0.04%).

(ii) Plants take up carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and form organic compounds during photosynthesis. These organic compounds are transferred to animals as food.

(iii) The carbon dioxide returns to the atmosphere during respiration, decay and
combustion of plants and animals.

(iv) The organic compounds of plants and animals are buried in the deep soil where they are acted upon by decomposers to change them to petroleum, coal, oil and carbonate rocks. These substances on their combustion release carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.

(v) Some carbon dioxide is found in the dissolved state in water. This gets converted to calcium carbonate in limestone. The weathering and combustion of carbonate-containing rocks or treatment of their minerals give CO2.

(vi) The hot springs and volcanic eruptions also give out CO2 in the atmosphere.

questions.q: Describe pyramid of energy with the help of diagram.
questions.solution:
1. A pyramid of energy is always upright. It can never be inverted because when energy flows from a particular trophic level, only 10% passes on as net energy to the next trophic level, and a large amount of energy is always lost as heat at each step.
  2. In smaller food chains, more energy is available than in the longer food chains.
  3. There are chain limitations of ecological pyramids. It assumes a simple food chain, something that almost never exists in nature.
  4. It does not accommodate a food web. Moreover, saprophytes are not given any place in ecological pyramids, even though they play a vital role in the ecosystem.

questions.q:
What is ecological succession?



Name various seral stages from pioneer species to climax community with suitable examples in hydrarch succession.
questions.solution:
The gradual and predictable change in the species composition of a given area is called ecological succession.



The following are the different seral stages in hydrach succession from pioneer species to climax community:

  1. Small phytoplankton are the primary successional species in aquatic settings.
  2. Phytoplankton are gradually replaced by rooted-submerged plants (e.g. Hydrilla), rooted-floating angiosperms (e.g. Lotus), free-floating plants (e.g. Pistia), reed swamp (e.g. Typha), marsh-meadow (e.g. Cyperus), scrub (e.g. Alnus), and finally trees (e.g. Quercus).
  3. The climax community would be a forest. The sea body transforms into land throughout time.
